newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end higher, News Corp stars.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end higher, News Corp stars.

text.p: The Australian share market punched its way back above the 2,500 level to close higher on Tuesday as enthusiastic buyers came out of the woodwork.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 18.2 points to 2,500.8.

While a surge in the Dow and metals prices set the early upbeat tone, media giant News Corp led the charge in the afternoon, rising more than 5.5 percent to A$7.09 (US$5.50), after it announced an alliance with EchoStar Communications Corp.
The alliance sees News Corp take 50 percent of EchoStar and contribute assets of US$1 billion to the joint venture.

Investors gave the deal the thumbs-up and jumped into News Corp ordinary and preferred ordinary stock, with News Corp turnover by value topping A$120 million, over 10 percent of the day's total turnover.
"They certainly impressed in the afternoon but the market has been solid all day," said a Sydney broker, pointing to the active trading levels seen on the day.
"There was plenty to go around with some good volumes."
Other traders agreed, saying the market had been marching to an upbeat tempo right from the start.
"The fundamentals looked good for today's trading with the strong U.S. market and generally better commodity prices," said a dealer at a Melbourne-based brokerage.
Biotech group Biota saw plenty of interest, up 45 cents to A$4.55 after Monday's announcement that trials of its anti-influenza drug would start in Australia in May.
Against the trend in the resource leaders, was Woodside Petroleum, which lost 28.5 cents to A$8.745 after crude oil futures hit their lowest level since August.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
